results.test_result: No unit test is possible. The bug sits in the macOS AppKit termination path inside the tao, muda and tauri-runtime-wry crates, which vitest cannot exercise. Traced against the crate sources pinned in src-tauri/Cargo.lock (tao 0.37.2, muda 0.20.0, tauri 2.12.5, tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.3).
results.reasoning: Rust side: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:195 adds the predefined `.quit()` item to the app menu. muda-0.20.0 src/platform_impl/macos/mod.rs:944 maps PredefinedMenuItemType::Quit to `sel!(terminate:)`, and src/items/predefined.rs:669 binds Cmd+Q to it. tao-0.37.2 src/platform_impl/macos/app_delegate.rs:47-89 declares the full delegate class: it implements applicationWillTerminate: (61-63) but not applicationShouldTerminate:, so AppKit takes its default answer, NSTerminateNow, and Quit cannot be cancelled. application_will_terminate (130-133) calls AppState::exit() (app_state.rs:271-281), which sends Event::LoopDestroyed. tauri-runtime-wry lib.rs:4131-4133 turns that into RunEvent::Exit. The two ExitRequested sites in that file (4262, 4302) come from the last window being destroyed and from app.exit(), not from terminate:. I grepped tao, tauri, tauri-runtime-wry and wry for ShouldTerminate, terminate: and quit Apple-event handlers and found nothing that hooks Quit. tao only sends CloseRequested from windowShouldClose: (window_delegate.rs:203), and AppKit's terminate: does not call windowShouldClose: on plain, non-document windows (from memory of Apple's NSApplication docs, not re-fetched). lib.rs:353 calls `.run(generate_context!())` with no RunEvent callback. JS side: the only flush-on-exit is registerCloseHandler (tauri-listeners.service.ts:50-80, wired in +layout.svelte:45) on `onCloseRequested`. There is no beforeunload or pagehide handler and no save on blur: registerFocusListener only refreshes the daily note. Autosave is a trailing debounce with no maxWait (debounce.ts:9-17; 2000 ms body, 500 ms frontmatter, editor.service.ts:196-200), and a failed save only re-arms a 5 s retry (editor.service.ts:181-194). So on Cmd+Q, Dock Quit or logout, tab.content that has not been written yet is lost with the process. Attempts to refute: I looked for a Rust RunEvent handler, a plugin that hooks terminate, a JS unload handler and a focus-loss save. None exist. Window close (red button) does go through CloseRequested and is safe.
results.corrections: Mostly accurate. Three points are narrower or unverified. (1) UpdateSection.svelte:208-210 `relaunch()` also skips the save, but it is only reachable from the Settings > Update panel after an update, so it is far rarer than Cmd+Q. (2) I did not verify the WebContent-process-crash reload claim (tauri-runtime-wry lib.rs:5053-5064). (3) Nothing was run on a device. The loss window is only edits not yet written: typed within the last 2 s (500 ms for frontmatter), or since the last 2 s pause during continuous typing, plus tabs stuck in a failed-save retry. Content already autosaved is safe.
results.fix_sketch: Pick one of two options. (a) Rust: call `.build(ctx)?.run(|app, ev| ...)` and, on macOS, intercept quit before AppKit commits. Swap the predefined `.quit()` for a custom 'Quit' MenuItem with the CmdOrCtrl+Q accelerator whose handler emits a `app-quit-requested` event to the main window. The JS side reuses the registerCloseHandler body (saveAllDirtyTabs, prompt on failures, drainEventCalendarWrites, flushSettingsPersistence) and then calls `exit()` from plugin-process. Dock Quit and logout still send terminate: directly, so also add an applicationShouldTerminate: override on the tao delegate class: return NSTerminateLater, emit the same event, and reply when JS calls back. (b) Cheaper partial fix: add maxWait to the body debounce so unsaved data is bounded. In UpdateSection.restartApp, await saveAllDirtyTabs() (and prompt on failure) before relaunch().

results.test_result: I mounted the real EditorView.svelte in jsdom, typed into a canvas text card (TextNode handleInput -> updateNodeData, which arms the 300 ms timer and pendingPersist), then switched tabs inside the window. 'F5: canvas -> note switch' PASSES. The note keeps its original content and the canvas tab gets the edit, so the onDestroy flush did run and landed in the canvas. 'F5 (close variant)' (closeActiveTab) also PASSES: the note is untouched. A different bug showed up and its test FAILS: 'F5 side effect: Cmd+W inside the 300 ms window either prompts or saves the canvas edit' fails with `expected false to be true`. No write to Board-1.canvas and no ask() prompt, so the edit is silently dropped.
results.reasoning: The chain the report describes exists. CanvasInner.svelte:230-233 onDestroy -> persistChanges -> onJsonChange = onContentChange (EditorView.svelte:81) -> editorStore.updateContent writes tabs[activeIndex] (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88) with no tab identity. The guard is in Svelte itself. Svelte 5.57.2 records the value a source had before its first write in the current flush (sources.js:189-196, old_values). While a teardown runs, `get()` returns that old value (runtime.js:651-652, is_destroying_effect is set in effects.js:450). onDestroy runs as an effect teardown. So when the {#if isCanvasTab} branch is torn down after setActiveIndex, removeTab or addTab, `activeIndex` reads its OLD value (the canvas index), and `tabs[1]` / `tabs.length` read the old proxy values too. A probe logged `updateContent activeIndex=1` (the canvas) after setActiveIndex(0). The app does not enable Svelte async mode, so BranchManager.ensure commits synchronously in the first flush pass (branches.js:229-235), before any old_values.clear(). Every path the report lists changes activeIndex from an event handler or an async continuation, never from inside an effect: tab click, Cmd+Shift+[/], Cmd+W, the sidebar or quick switcher, a FileNode header click, and openFileInEditor for a new file after its await. So the old value is always captured. I grepped for $effect/onMount bodies that change the active tab and for flushSync in src/lib, and found none that could run while a canvas is mounted. Same verdict for the duplicates F13, F20, F150 and F171: they are the same mechanism. F171(c), xyflow re-measuring on mount, only arms the same flush, which also lands in the canvas.
results.corrections: The core claim, canvas JSON written into the newly active note, does not happen with the current Svelte version. It is protected only by Svelte's teardown old-value semantics, which is fragile and undocumented as a contract. A different, smaller bug is real (F20 hints at it): on Cmd+W or closeTab within 300 ms of a canvas edit, the canvas tab is not dirty in the store, so closeTab does not prompt. removeTab then runs and the onDestroy flush writes into the removed tab object (old index), so the last edit is silently lost. This is reproduced by the 'F5 side effect' test. It loses at most about 300 ms of canvas typing.
results.fix_sketch: Do not rely on Svelte teardown semantics. Pass the tab path into CanvasView and CanvasInner, and make persist call a path-keyed writer (editorStore.updateTabContentOnly(path, json) + scheduleAutoSave) instead of onContentChange. For close: flush the pending canvas persist before removeTab, for example from a tab-close hook in closeTab called before the dirty check, so the edit is saved or the user is prompted.

results.test_result: 'F21: an edit typed <300 ms before a canvas-to-canvas switch is kept in the first canvas' FAILS: `expected '{..."text": "card A"...}' to contain 'last words'`. Board-1's edit is never persisted. 'F21 (stale flag)' PASSES: leaving Board-2 for a note does not write into the note. 'F21 (shared undo history)' FAILS: with no edit at all, Cmd+Z right after switching Board-1 -> Board-2 sets Board-2's tab content to Board-1's JSON (`expected ... not to contain 'card A'`).
results.reasoning: EditorView.svelte:80-81 renders both canvas tabs in the same unkeyed {#if} branch, so CanvasView and CanvasInner are reused and only jsonContent changes. The sync effect (CanvasInner.svelte:85-98) sets syncing=true and replaces nodes. The debounce effect (212-226) re-runs: its teardown clearTimeout cancels Board-1's pending persist, and its body returns at line 218 because syncing is true. Board-1's store content was never updated, so the edit is gone (reproduced). pendingPersist stays true, as the report says. But the later onDestroy flush it predicts lands in Board-2 (the old activeIndex during teardown, same Svelte old_values mechanism as in F5), so it never reaches the note (test passes). While tracing, I found a worse consequence of the reused instance. `history` (line 101) is never reset, and the sync effect pushes Board-2's baseline onto Board-1's stack (line 94). Cmd+Z in Board-2 (handleKeydown 261-271) undoes to Board-1's snapshot and calls persistWithoutHistory -> onContentChange. Board-2's tab becomes Board-1's nodes, and the 2 s body autosave writes that into Board-2.canvas on disk.
results.corrections: The stale persist flag is real but harmless: it flushes into Board-2 itself, not into another tab. The dropped edit only covers about the last 300 ms of typing. The more serious bug in the same mechanism, which the report missed, is the shared undo history across canvases. Undo right after a canvas-to-canvas switch overwrites the second canvas with the first one's content and autosaves it. Redo or file history can recover it.
results.fix_sketch: Key the canvas branch by tab path ({#key editorStore.activeTab.path}<CanvasView .../>{/key}), so each canvas gets a fresh CanvasInner with its own history and its own onDestroy flush. Combine that with the path-keyed persist from F5, so the flush during destroy targets the right file without relying on Svelte teardown semantics.

Keystrokes run synchronously through the CM updateListener (editor-extensions.ts:170-188) into onContentChange, then editorStore.updateContent (editor.store.svelte.ts:84-88), and arm debouncedSave. An aggravating fact the original misses: the 'edit' source pushes the BUFFER into the Rust index after a 1 s pause (note-change.service.ts:88, rust:'deduped'). So the Tasks tab can list tasks and line numbers from unsaved text, while Rust toggles that line number on DISK. A shifted line can tick the wrong task on disk (the F140 note is correct), and the buffer is then replaced as well. F6/F14/F76/F127/F140/F152/F156/F160/F181 describe the same root cause.
results.corrections: Mostly accurate. The 'lineNumber comes from the disk version' remark in F152 is wrong: the index follows the buffer after 1 s of idle via the 'edit' source, so lines can disagree with disk, and that makes it worse (wrong-line toggle). The dirty window covers more than 2 s after the last keystroke in A: any keystroke in any tab restarts the shared debounce, and a failing save keeps the tab dirty (5 s retry loop), as F160 and F152 note. Deep-link overwrite (deep-link.service.ts:298) is an explicit replacement and should not count as the same bug.
results.fix_sketch: In toggleTask, when an open tab for filePath is dirty, flush it first with `await saveFileByPath(filePath)` and abort with a toast if the save fails, then call toggle_task_status. The alternative is to toggle the line in tab.content on the TS side and save. In general, syncExternalContentToEditor(markSaved=true) should refuse, or merge, when the tab is dirty and the caller built its content from disk.

results.test_result: Both F45 cases FAIL on the bug assertion. Dirty tab: `expected 'see [[Z]] draft' to contain 'more'`. Clean tab: `expected 'see [[Z]]' to contain 'more'`. In both cases the sanity check (content has [[Z]]) passed. writeTextFile/readTextFile were deferred, and onContentChange ran during the await.
results.reasoning: link-updater.service.ts:33-35 snapshots openTab.content (dirty) or awaits readTextFile (clean). :39 awaits writeTextFile. :47 syncExternalContentToEditor(..., true, 'none') then calls updateTabContentByPath with no check that tab.content still equals the snapshot. For the active tab, bumpExternalContentSignal makes MarkdownEditor (311-337) replace the whole doc with addToHistory(false). The user renames X in the explorer or a menu, so focus is outside the editor. To lose text they must click back into Y and type before Y's read or write IPC settles. For a note with a few backlinks that is a few ms, too fast for a human. If tab.content !== the snapshot (the content used to build updatedContent), re-apply replaceWikilinks to the current tab.content and keep it dirty (markSaved=false, schedule 'body'), or skip the sync. results.test_result: No test written. results.reasoning: reloadExternallyChangedTabs (editor.service.ts:378-381) drops dirty tabs, records nothing and shows no notice. saveFileByPath (:161-178) writes tab.content unconditionally, with no mtime or hash precondition. The debounce is purely trailing, with no maxWait (debounce.ts), so a tab stays dirty through a whole typing session with pauses under 2 s, and through a failing save (5 s retry at :191-193). File history snapshots only on app saves: registerFileHistoryHook uses addAfterSaveObserver (file-history.service.ts:190-195), so the external version is never captured. The only other caller of reloadExternallyChangedTabs is the watcher batch (app-lifecycle.service.ts:486), and nothing reloads on focus. No ADR or doc records the policy: I grepped docs/ and CONTEXT.md. A sequencing detail confirms the loss even when the autosave runs before the watcher: if the last keystroke was 1.5 s before the external write, the autosave fires at about +0.5 s, before the reload at about +0.8 s. Disk then equals savedContent and the reload does nothing. Reachable whenever another writer (iCloud/Obsidian Sync from a phone, git pull, an AI agent editing the vault, a script) touches the note the user is actively editing.
results.corrections: Accurate. The original itself notes this is by design, not an oversight. It is real, silent loss of externally written content, but fixing it means a product decision (conflict UI or merge), not a one-line fix.
results.fix_sketch: When reloadExternallyChangedTabs skips a dirty tab whose disk content differs from savedContent, record the divergence: store the disk text and mark the tab 'conflicted'. Before the next save, either do a 3-way merge (base = savedContent, ours = content, theirs = disk) or ask the user, and snapshot the external version to file history before overwriting.

Each further Backspace deletes another character of the note, possibly off-screen. With a selection elsewhere, Delete or Backspace removes the whole selection. Tab runs indentWithTab on the selected line, Enter on a focused toggle or select inserts a newline, and Mod-z undoes editor history. The 2 s autosave then writes the damaged note. results.scenario: The user types `^[` on a line. closeBrackets makes it `^[]` with the cursor between the brackets. The user then clicks or arrows to another line before typing the footnote text. Opening any note that contains `^[]` off the cursor line does the same: for example a regex like `s/^[]//` in prose or inline code, since only the node at line start is checked for block context. buildFootnoteDecorations reaches the inline-footnote branch and calls footnoteRefDeco.range(start+2, start+2). CodeMirror throws RangeError: Mark decorations may not be empty. The throw happens inside the ViewPlugin update or constructor, so CodeMirror logs it and deactivates the plugin. view.plugin(footnotePlugin) becomes null, and every `[^1]` ref, footnote definition and `^[...]` inline footnote stops rendering. The EditorView is shared across tabs, so the breakage lasts across note switches until the live-preview extensions are rebuilt. No text is lost, but the editor silently degrades and the error reaches the exception sink (console / Sentry).

results.reasoning: Refutation attempts. (1) Does the reveal rule save it? Only while the cursor is on that line. Any selection move off the line, or opening a note with `^[]` elsewhere, reaches the push. (2) Does the regex reject empty content? No: `([^\]\\]*...)` matches zero characters. (3) Is the throw caught? CodeMirror catches ViewPlugin exceptions only to log them and deactivate the plugin, which the test shows by view.plugin() returning null. (4) Is it known? results.fix_sketch: In buildFootnoteDecorations, push the text mark only when range.textTo > range.textFrom, or skip empty inline footnotes entirely (`if (range.textFrom === range.textTo) continue;`). restoreSnapshot rethrows at src/lib/features/file-history/file-history.service.ts:101-104, and its only caller FileHistoryDialog.svelte:50 sits in handleRestore (:40-51) with no try/catch or toast. No unhandledrejection handler exists in src. error() (src/lib/utils/debug.ts:27-33) only logs and reports to Sentry, so the user sees nothing, and fileHistoryStore.reset() at service :100 is skipped, leaving the dialog open. Side note, outside this finding: saveFileByPath returns false instead of throwing on a failed write (src/lib/core/editor/editor.service.ts:167-177), so restoreSnapshot still resets the store after a failed save.

The closing-fence rule differs by reader. findFrontmatterBlock uses FRONTMATTER_FENCE_RE = /^---\s*$/ (src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/live-preview/parsers/frontmatter.ts:10, 17-32), which rejects `----`. frontmatterSlice accepts any line starting with `---` (core/frontmatter-slice.ts:16), and the properties regex in src/lib/core/frontmatter/properties.logic.ts:37 also accepts it, so the sidebar shows properties. computeFrontmatter (plugins/frontmatter-field.ts:12-25) is wired in live-preview.ts:46 and hides lines 1..closeIdx with hideLines and no reveal check, so a later exact `---` hides body text. No guard prevents it. Display-only; no write path. The fence test at src/lib/core/markdown-editor/setup/editor-extensions.ts:174-177 also uses the exact-fence rule.

applyPathChange (src/lib/core/filesystem/path-change.service.ts:117-132) awaits diskOp() before updateTabAfterRenameOrMove, and closeTabsForDeletedPath runs only for deletes (:125). moveItem (src/lib/core/filesystem/fs.service.ts:228-240) and auto-move (src/lib/features/auto-move/auto-move.service.ts:188) flush no pending save. saveFileByPath (src/lib/core/editor/editor.service.ts:161-168) reads tab.path when the timer fires and calls writeTextFile with no options; the Rust default is create:true, truncate:true (tauri-plugin-fs-2.7.1 src/commands.rs:1166-1180). markSavedByPath (editor.store.svelte.ts:91-96) matches by path, so the write-then-rename race leaves a ghost at the old path and the moved tab dirty. The exact write/rename ordering is runtime behavior and was not reproduced, but neither IPC is ordered by the TS side, so the race is not blocked by any barrier.

renameItem short-circuits only on exact equality (src/lib/core/filesystem/fs.service.ts:204), then throws targetExistsError when exists(newPath) is true (:205). Tauri plugin-fs 2.7.1 (the version pinned in src-tauri/Cargo.lock) implements exists as PathBuf::exists (~/.cargo/registry/.../tauri-plugin-fs-2.7.1/src/commands.rs:1262-1274), so a case variant on default case-insensitive APFS reports true; the only case-insensitive comparison, link-updater.service.ts:25, skips link rewriting and does not guard the rename. The APFS behaviour is OS-level and was not reproduced here. FilesNavigator.svelte:147 and NoteRowMenu.svelte:102 reach the same check.

Snapshots are keyed only by file_path: save_snapshot and get_file_history (src-tauri/src/commands/history.rs:57-84), find_latest_hash and list_snapshots (src-tauri/src/db/history_repo.rs:18-26, 46-50). No path-change consumer touches history: the registrations in app/boot.ts, event-calendar, files-navigator and neighbourhood do not include it, and applyPathChange (path-change.service.ts:107-125) never re-keys rows. The mechanism is confirmed. The 'silent' framing is overstated, since FileHistoryDialog.svelte:44-50 asks for confirmation and the diff view shows the change; the JSON's severity 'medium' is also higher than the verifier's 'low' supports.

extractBlockContent uses line.includes(`^${blockId}`) with no boundary check (src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/live-preview/embed-resolver.logic.ts:41, 45), so '^abc' matches an earlier line ending in '^abcdef', and the trailing-token strip at :46 returns 'first point'. The caller widgets.ts:576 passes blockId through unchanged, and no guard exists. The navigation path disagrees: findBlockIdPosition (extensions/wikilink/navigation.logic.ts:36-44) requires an exact match on the BLOCK_ID_RE capture, so an embed and a jump can point at different lines.

CRLF: no EditorState.lineSeparator is set anywhere in src/lib (grep returns none), so CodeMirror's toString joins lines with '\n' (node_modules/@codemirror/state/dist/index.js:106, 179). editor-extensions.ts:188 sends doc.toString() and editor.service.ts:168 writes it, so the first edit saves the whole file as LF. Properties: rebuildContent hardcodes '\n' (properties.logic.ts:621) over a body that keeps CRLF. BOM: plugin-fs readTextFile decodes with the default TextDecoder, which strips U+FEFF (node_modules/@tauri-apps/plugin-fs/dist-js/index.js:498), so the tab starts without it. The Rust toggle keeps it: read_to_string at src-tauri/src/commands/vault.rs:669, toggle_task_in_content only rewrites one line (src-tauri/src/vault/parsing.rs:1873-1900), updated_content returned at vault.rs:687, and tasks.service.ts:114 passes it unchanged into syncExternalContentToEditor (editor.service.ts:70). FRONTMATTER_REGEX (properties.logic.ts:37) is anchored at ^--- and no U+FEFF handling exists in src/lib or src-tauri/src, so the second-block failure follows.

renameItem only renames the folder (fs.service.ts:201-212, diskOp at 211; FilesNavigator.svelte:153 also has no folder-note handling), and folderNoteDir returns null for Work/Projects.md (folder-notes.logic.ts:59-64), so the Work key is never added to contentOrder (folder-notes.logic.ts:47-56; fs.logic.ts:416-419 falls back to name order). The scenario's claim that findFolderNote has no callers is wrong: it is called at FilesNavigator.svelte:210 (pickFolder), so the folder-note click also stops opening after a rename, which is the real consequence.

selectSnapshot (file-history.service.ts:56-77) has no request token, and SnapshotList onclick (SnapshotList.svelte:40) is not disabled while isLoadingDiff, so the UI allows clicking A then B, and handleRestore reads selectedSnapshot (FileHistoryDialog.svelte:40-41). Whether A's setDiffLines can land after B's depends on IPC completion order, which reading cannot settle: get_snapshot_content and compute_diff are plain sync commands (history.rs:88, 95), which Tauri docs say run on the main thread, making the Rust side FIFO, so the interleaving looks unlikely in practice though not excluded by webview response ordering.

readNote is a raw readTextFile with no CRLF normalization (editor-host.ts:68-70), and HEADING_RE (embed-resolver.logic.ts:2) cannot match a line ending in \r because '.' excludes \r and '$' has no m flag, so extractHeadingSection returns null (lines 8-22). stripFrontmatter's check at line 60 fails on a \r after the closing delimiter, and extractHeadingSection does not track fenced code (lines 13-31), so a '# comment' inside a fence ends a level-2 section early. The only precondition is a CRLF or fenced-code note on disk, which the app does not guard against.

write_atomic writes a new temp file with std::fs::write and renames it over the target (utils/fs.rs:26-28), so the note gets a new inode with default mode and no xattr copy; there is no set_permissions, xattr or sync_all anywhere in src-tauri/src apart from an unrelated index_cache.rs:70. The temp file is removed only in the rename-failure branch (fs.rs:29-31), not when the write at line 26 fails, and read_file_metadata takes created() from the new inode on each index update (vault.rs:233-247, 286), which feeds ctime at vault.rs:789 after toggle_task (vault.rs:683-685). The read-only guard (fs.rs:20-24) is real but does not preserve mode.

getFileNameError only forbids <>:"/\|?* (fs.logic.ts:117-124, set at :121), and the rename gate FilesNavigator.svelte:148 uses it with no other guard, so '#', '[' and ']' reach replaceWikilinks, which writes newName raw ('[[' + newName, link-updater.logic.ts:30; caller link-updater.service.ts:36). WIKILINK_RE (link-updater.logic.ts:8) does not match '[[C#]]' or '[[a]b]]', so a later rewrite skips them. Not checked: the Rust resolver's reading of these forms, and no tests were run.

findBackupTimestamp returns the first Set member within tolerance (file-history.logic.ts:168-172), not the nearest. The Set is filled in readDir order with no sort (file-history.service.ts:163-172), and FileHistoryDialog.svelte:34 uses it directly. Backup names use Date.now() after the IPC (service.ts:121), while snapshot timestamps are Rust created_at (history.rs:64), so two saves within 10 s can open a neighbour's backup. No guard found; the impact is limited to the Reveal in Finder target. Tests not run.

MERMAID_OPEN_RE and QUERYJS_OPEN_RE are anchored at column 0 (parsers/mermaid.ts:19, parsers/queryjs-block.ts:19) and tested against the whole opening line (fenced-code-block.ts:132). code-block-field.ts:27 skips the same languages using the Lezer CodeInfo language, so an indented or blockquoted fence gets neither the special renderer nor the generic code widget. The column-0 rule is a documented design choice, but no fallback exists. Tests not run.

The open_vault_db catch returns at app-lifecycle.service.ts:237, before registerFileHistoryHook (:268), unsubscribeFileChange assignment (:494), startWatching (:499) and loadDirectoryTree (:315). The gate at :172 is then false on the next switch. The only reloadExternallyChangedTabs caller is the watcher batch (:486), and editor.service.ts has no mtime or conflict check on save. Two overstatements: 'editor fully usable' is wrong (no file tree, no step 5-9), and the carry-over is only tabs opened during the failed session, since A's tabs are reset by teardownVault's resetEditor (:622) when B's init starts. The verifier's repro asserting A's tab survives would therefore fail. Tests not run.

updateLinksAfterRename awaits call('get_backlinks_v2') with no try/catch (src/lib/core/filesystem/link-updater.service.ts:27). applyPathChange awaits it unguarded (path-change.service.ts:149) before refreshTree (:153) and rename_note/forgetNote sweep (:159, :168-170), and renameItem rethrows after diskOp has already moved the file (fs.service.ts:206-218). get_backlinks_v2 returns Err only on a poisoned RwLock (commands/vault.rs:431-441, VaultIndexState is an RwLock per src-tauri/src/vault/mod.rs:25). No caller or guard prevents the abort. The docstring at path-change.service.ts:111 ('Never throws on the index legs') contradicts the code. Trigger is rare (poisoned lock only). I did not verify the exact user-facing 'Could not rename' text.

compute_diff pushes a DiffLine with DiffLineType::Equal for every unchanged line, with no context limit or hunk filtering (src-tauri/src/commands/history.rs:95-135, Equal branch 103-112). The only caller, selectSnapshot (src/lib/features/file-history/file-history.service.ts:65-71), stores the full array without filtering. DiffViewer.svelte:41-52 renders each entry as a <tr> with four <td> cells inside a plain table, with no virtualization. Nothing caps the input size. The impact is a performance/freeze risk on very large notes, not data loss, and the 'slow' claim is unmeasured.

BLOCK_TAGS (src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/live-preview/handlers/paste-html-link.logic.ts:21-26) includes TABLE and TR but not TD or TH, so blockAwareText (:34-57) concatenates cell text with no separator. htmlLinksToMarkdown (:68-97) returns converted text whenever an anchor URL is absent from text/plain (:75-79). paste-html-link-handler.ts:27-28 returns that string as-is, and the handler is registered before pasteTsvHandler (live-preview.ts:101), so the TSV path never runs for such a paste. The existing tests (src/tests/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/live-preview/handlers/paste-html-link.logic.test.ts) have no table-cell case. I did not run the replay.
